{"type":"text","timestamp":1793303184602,"sessionID":"ses_e76cd4c9fffeedy2e1o3py4GiN","part":{"id":"prt_18933047c001srqLpxrCzu0019","sessionID":"ses_e76cd4c9fffeedy2e1o3py4GiN","messageID":"msg_18932e637001aJVeZm5FHX6z8t","type":"text","text":"I wrote one primer pair to `primers.fasta`. A single pair is enough because the only difference between the plasmids is one contiguous insertion. I did not run the primers through the NEB kit or a PCR simulation. I checked the design only by confirming that the template with the insert spliced in matches the output sequence exactly.\n\n**The edit:** the output plasmid has a 39 bp insertion, `tagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaaag`. It sits after `...atatacatatgag` and before `caagggcgaggag...` at position 215 of the input.\n\n**The design:** this is the standard Q5 site-directed mutagenesis layout for an insertion. The forward primer carries the insert as a 5' tail, and the two primers sit back to back without overlapping. The pair amplifies the whole plasmid.\n\n```\n>fwd\ntagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaaagcaagggcgaggagctgtt\n>rev\nctcatatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttcta\n```\n\n| Primer | Annealing part | Annealing length | Tm (oligotm, flags as specified) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| fwd | `caagggcgaggagctgtt` (after the 39 nt tail) | 18 nt | 63.81 °C |\n| rev | the whole primer, reverse complement of the sequence upstream of the insertion point | 45 nt | 63.81 °C |\n\nThe two Tms differ by about 0.003 °C. Both annealing lengths are within 15–45 nt, and both Tms are within 58–72 °C. Tm was calculated on the annealing portion only, as you specified.\n\nThe reverse primer uses the full 45 nt allowed. Among the pairs that met the rules, I picked the one with the closest Tm match and then the shortest combined annealing length.","time":{"start":1793303184601,"end":1793303184601}}}
